_comment: All costs in USD. Edit these before quoting anything to management — every number here is an assumption, not a measurement. Fields marked SOURCE:QUOTE must be replaced with a real vendor quote.

usage._note: active_student_ratio: not every enrolled student uses the AI every day. 0.75 is a planning guess — instrument the pilot and replace it.

tokens._note: writing_samples=3 is the self-consistency setting in scoring/client.py. Input is re-sent per sample, so cloud cost scales linearly with it unless prompt caching is used.

cloud._note: SOURCE:QUOTE — placeholder rates for a MID-TIER hosted model plus hosted ASR/TTS. Replace with your actual contracted rates. This single field decides the whole purchase: at these rates hosted inference costs ~$104/month at peak load and on-prem never pays back. Run `--voice isolate_llm` and read the price-boundary section: GPUs only win above ~17x these rates, i.e. frontier-model pricing. If band scoring genuinely needs a frontier model, re-quote here first. cache_hit_ratio applies to the shared rubric system prompt, which is large and identical across every request.

local._note: electricity_per_kwh 0.19 reflects Philippine commercial rates, which are high — this is why PUE and powered-hours matter more here than they would in Korea. gpu_watts_avg is the average draw under mixed load, not TDP.

throughput._note: tokens_per_second_output: aggregate output throughput for Gemma 4 26B A4B (MoE, ~4B active) on one RTX 5090 at Q4 under continuous batching. SOURCE:QUOTE — measure before purchase. NOTE: at the modelled volume this assumption does NOT bind. One box serves ~599M output tokens/month against ~78M of demand, so fleet size is set entirely by the one-box-per-campus redundancy floor. Halving or doubling throughput changes nothing (verified in the sensitivity sweep). It only starts to matter above roughly 8x the current student load. utilisation_ceiling accounts for peak-hour bunching: everyone submits at the end of class, not uniformly across the day.

staff._note: human_review_rate: fraction of AI scores routed to a human by the self-consistency spread gate plus random audit. This cost exists in BOTH scenarios — it is not a differentiator — but it is modelled so the total cost of running the service is visible.
